newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat orders inquiry into Palestinian corruption.
newsitem.headline: Arafat orders inquiry into Palestinian corruption.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has ordered an inquiry into an auditor's report that members of his administration squandered $326 million in public funds last year, the official Palestinian news agency said on Thursday.
The agency WAFA said the eight-member team, due to be headed by the secretary-general of Arafat's office, Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, was given a month to complete its report.

"President Yasser Arafat...issued an order establishing a national investigation committee to probe what came in the report by the head of the General Monitoring Institution in the National Authority," WAFA said.
Two weeks ago the General Monitoring Institution, an audit office set up by Arafat, said in a 600-page report that $326 million in public funds were mismanaged or squandered last year.

It was the first official criticism of corruption within the administration since self-rule began in 1994. It followed increasing complaints by Palestinians and lawmakers against alleged corruption and mismanagement.
Palestinian lawmakers have accused the Palestinian Authority of putting taxpayers' money into villas and cars for ministers and other senior officials.
WAFA said that apart from Abdel-Rahim, the investigation team includes a high court judge, two businessmen, two academics and two members of the PLO executive committee.
A copy of the report, which has yet to be made public, was handed over to Arafat. Palestinian officials have said five ministers in Arafat's cabinet were named in the report.
